notes: Four reviewed policy questions from the VOTER panel, 2016–2020. Wave-specific cross-sectional estimates; repeated panelists are not independent samples. January 2019 includes late-2018 interviews. No missing years are estimated. Earlier 2011 responses and other questions are not included in this pilot.

entries.title: Abortion legality
entries.question: Do you think abortion should be...
entries.question_note: Legal in all cases = +1; legal in some cases = 0; illegal in all cases = −1. The midpoint represents conditional legality, not necessarily ideological centrism. Unknown, skipped and not-asked answers are excluded. Wave-specific cross-sectional weights are used.

entries.title: Gun control laws
entries.question: Do you think gun control laws should be made more or less strict than they are now?
entries.question_note: More strict = +1; no change = 0; less strict = −1. No change is a status-quo answer, not necessarily ideological centrism. Unknown, skipped and not-asked answers are excluded. Wave-specific cross-sectional weights are used.

entries.title: Health insurance mandate
entries.question: As you may know, the Affordable Care Act required nearly all Americans to have health insurance, or else pay a fine. Congress passed a law repealing this requirement starting in January 2019. Do you favor or oppose requiring all Americans have health insurance?
entries.question_note: Strongly favor = +1; somewhat favor = +1/3; somewhat oppose = −1/3; strongly oppose = −1. This asks about an insurance requirement, not government-run insurance. The January 2019 wave was fielded November 17, 2018–January 7, 2019 and is plotted under its named wave year. Unknown, skipped and not-asked answers are excluded. Wave-specific cross-sectional weights are used.
